verdict.rationale: E2B documents continuous sandbox sessions of up to 24 hours on Pro (1 hour on Base), with an adjustable timeout via setTimeout/set_timeout. For multi-day work it directs users to pause and resume, which preserves filesystem, memory and running processes, and paused sandboxes are kept indefinitely. Hours are covered on Pro, but days of continuous running are not; long tasks must be split by pause/resume. Missing for 10: continuous runtime beyond 24 hours, long sessions on the Base tier, independent or hands-on corroboration of multi-hour or multi-day agent runs.

support.subject: As a developer, I can keep a sandbox session running for hours or days for long agent tasks

citations.quote: Sandboxes can run continuously for up to 24 hours (Pro) or 1 hour (Base). For longer workloads, use pause and resume
You can change the sandbox timeout when it's running by calling the `setTimeout` method in JavaScript or `set_timeout` method in Python.
Pause a sandbox and resume it later from the exact state it was in, including the filesystem and the memory, so running processes and loaded variables survive.
A paused sandbox is kept indefinitely with no automatic deletion.
